headline: Steady rain and the season's first widespread Cascade snow arrive tonight into Wednesday, then cool showers linger before drying this weekend.
summary: As of Tuesday evening, showers turn to steadier rain tonight and continue into Wednesday morning, with southwest winds of 20 to 30 mph, mainly in the Southwest Interior through Shelton. A Winter Weather Advisory covers all the Cascade zones until 5 PM Wednesday for the first widespread mountain snow of the season. Snow levels start around 4000 to 4500 feet and fall to 3000 to 3500 feet by Wednesday morning. Forecasters expect about 4 to 8 inches at Stevens Pass, 1 to 3 inches at Snoqualmie Pass, and around 6 to 12 inches in the southern Cascades, including White Pass and Paradise. Travelers should check WSDOT for road conditions. After the front passes, a pocket of cold air high in the atmosphere (an upper low) lingers over western Washington into late week. That brings spotty showers and highs in the low to mid 50s Wednesday and Thursday. Showers continue Friday, with light snow still possible in the Cascades. The system slowly moves out over the weekend, giving drier weather into early next week, with weekend highs in the mid 50s. Overnight lows may approach the low to mid 30s, so forecasters are watching for possible frost or freezing conditions and will keep monitoring that threat. The exact timing of the drying depends on how quickly the system leaves.
changes: The early-morning discussions described a slow-moving upper low with showers and mountain snow, with Cascade snow of up to 4 inches tonight and 4 more Wednesday. By afternoon the forecast stressed a front bringing steadier rain tonight, with specific snow totals for individual passes and a southern Cascades total of 6 to 12 inches. The evening update kept the afternoon forecast unchanged.
